class.name: PolyMeshBuilderND
class.brief_description: Functions for creating and modifying N-dimensional polytope meshes.
class.description: PolyMeshBuilderND is a singleton for creating and modifying N-dimensional polytope meshes. It contains all functions important enough to be included in the ND module, but too complex to be included in [ArrayPolyMeshND], and not important enough to have their own dedicated types. For example, creating a box is handled by [BoxPolyMeshND], not by this class.

method.name: convert_mesh_3d_to_nd_faces_only
method.description: Converts a 3D [Mesh] into a 3-dimensional [ArrayPolyMeshND] by copying the vertex positions, inferring the edges of faces, and translating the faces to use those edges. Since the result is a 3-dimensional mesh, the faces are its boundary cells, so the face normals become the boundary normals, the 3D mesh's vertex normals become the boundary cell vertex normals, and the 3D mesh's UVs become the 2-dimensional cell texture map. If [param which_surface] is -1, then all surfaces are used, otherwise the specified surface is used. If [param deduplicate] is true, then vertices and edges will be deduplicated so that vertices with the same position will be merged into a single vertex, otherwise separate vertices and edges in the input will be kept separate. The resulting mesh will only have the 2D faces brought in with as minimal modifications as possible. After conversion, the mesh can be further modified with other functions in this class, such as extruding it into a higher dimension with [method extrude_linear].

method.name: delete_interior
method.description: Deletes the interior of a poly mesh, meaning any interior boundary cells shared by two volumes, as well as all volumes and all higher-dimensional elements. For an N-dimensional mesh, the volumes are its N-dimensional cells, and the boundary cells are its (N-1)-dimensional cells, such as 3D cells in a 4D mesh, faces in a 3D mesh, or edges in a 2D mesh. This operates on [param mesh_nd], in place, turning a solid poly mesh into its boundary. Any boundary cells shared by two volumes are considered to be structural scaffolding on the interior of the mesh. These cells do not result in any visible geometry and are not rendered. Returns the number of boundary cells deleted. A mesh without volumes is left unchanged. Any bindings associated with the deleted elements are also removed. This is the counterpart of [method extrude_linear] on a solid mesh, whose output has one volume per input volume and an interior boundary cell between each pair of adjacent input volumes.

method.name: extrude_linear
method.description: Extrudes a mesh into a higher dimension by creating 2 copies of the input mesh's data, translating one copy by the [param extrusion_vector] and the other copy by the negative of the [param extrusion_vector], and then connecting the corresponding cells of each dimension into new cells one dimension higher. If [param extrusion_vector] is empty, the default is to extrude one unit along a new axis one dimension above the input mesh, such as extruding a 3-dimensional mesh along the fourth axis. This operation is similar to Blender's "Mesh → Extrude → Extrude Faces" operation (hotkey "E"), but generalized to N dimensions, extruding cells of every dimension at once. Also, unlike Blender's operation, this function extrudes in both directions at once, and extrudes the entire mesh at once instead of allowing selection of which cells to extrude. When the extrusion adds a dimension, the input mesh's boundary normals, boundary cell vertex normals, and cell texture maps are carried over onto the cells extruded from the input's boundary cells. Without that data, if the input mesh has volumetric cells, the new boundary cells are oriented outward using them, and [method make_boundary_normals_topologically_consistent] is used with the two copies of the input mesh's boundary cells as the authoritative references. The input's normal and texture map bindings are also kept on the two copies, but nothing is derived for the new lower-dimensional elements, so the bindings below the output's boundary cells come out covering only the copies. [method ArrayPolyMeshND.delete_normals_below_dimension] and [method ArrayPolyMeshND.delete_texture_maps_below_dimension] remove them once they are no longer wanted, which for a texture map made for the input is usually right away. The input mesh MUST have 2D faces defined in [member ArrayPolyMeshND.poly_cell_indices] for any cells to be connected, meaning that [member ArrayPolyMeshND.poly_cell_indices] MUST have a length of at least 1, or else only the vertices and edges will be connected.

method.name: make_boundary_normals_topologically_consistent
method.description: Makes the boundary normals of an N-dimensional polytope mesh topologically consistent by ensuring that all boundary cells that share a common (N-2)-dimensional member have the same normal direction. The [param authoritative_boundary_cells] parameter specifies a list of boundary cell indices that are considered authoritative for determining the normal direction. Their normals will be preserved, and any adjacent non-authoritative boundary cells will be flipped if necessary to match the authoritative normals, recursively propagating in a flood-fill manner. [b]Note:[/b] This function only works correctly if the input mesh has star-shaped polytope boundary cells, and if it can locate a point within the star-shaped region of that cell. For non-convex cells, you may need to set [member ArrayPolyMeshND.poly_cell_boundary_pivot_overrides] to specify where the pivot point is located in the cells.

method.name: make_coplanar
method.description: Splits every element whose vertices do not lie in a flat space of its own dimension, such as a 2D plane for a 2D face, or a 3D hyperplane for a 3D cell. The resulting elements will be flat in the space. This is an in-place operation which modifies the given mesh. Returns how many splits were made. An element is flat when its vertices stay within [param angle_tolerance_radians] of such a flat, relative to its size. A split cuts off one vertex: the element's boundary is divided into the parts that have the vertex and the parts that do not, and a new element of the dimension below closes both sides, a diagonal edge for a face, a face through the surrounding edges for a 3D cell, and so on, so a face loses a triangle and a cell loses a pyramid. The vertex cut off is the one whose removal leaves the rest closest to flat, then the one standing farthest out of the flat through the rest, then the one with the smallest cut, so a box face with one corner raised is cut along its level diagonal into a flat triangle and a leaning one, and a polygon with one raised corner loses only that corner's triangle. Faces are split before cells, and a cut that is not flat itself is split in turn, so every dimension is flat once this returns. The pieces, the elements above them, and the bindings follow [method ArrayPolyMeshND.split_poly_element], which does the bookkeeping. The cross-sections that an N-dimensional mesh renders are only flat when its (N-1)-dimensional boundary cells are, and [method extrude_linear] gives flat cells only from flat input cells, which is what this is for.

method.name: merge_coplanar_faces
method.description: Merges adjacent 2D faces that lie in the same plane into single faces, in place, and returns how many merges were made. Two faces are merged when they share an edge, every vertex of one lies in the plane of the other within [param angle_tolerance_radians] (measured as the angle of each vertex's offset out of the plane), and the merged polygon is convex, since faces are triangulated as fans. The edges that were interior to the merged faces are deleted. This intentionally only operates on 2D faces, and does not merge cells of higher dimensions. It repairs faces that were needlessly split, such as quads triangulated by a glTF export and brought in through [method convert_mesh_3d_to_nd_faces_only]. For a 3D mesh, the faces are the boundary cells, so each merged face keeps the orientation, boundary normal, and pivot override of the faces it absorbed, and faces are not merged across seam edges or when they face opposite ways. For meshes of higher dimensions, the cells keep referencing the merged faces and keep their orientation and boundary normals. Every normal and texture map binding is carried over: each merged face takes its values from the faces it absorbed, and the bindings of edges and cells follow their surviving sub-elements. An element whose values cannot all be found in its sources, such as a face merged from a mapped and an unmapped triangle, ends up with an empty entry, meaning missing data. Faces must have their edges stored in loop order, which every built-in mesh source provides.

method.name: subdivide_elements
method.description: Subdivides the selected elements of the given dimension, in place, returning the indices of the new elements created from the selected ones, so that callers can keep track of the inputs, such as updating a user's selection in a modeling tool. If [param elements] is empty, all elements of the given dimension are subdivided. Repeat the subdivision for finer detail. The subdivision splits all edges at their midpoints, and uses well-proportioned decompositions per shape: triangles subdivide into 4 similar triangles, other polygons subdivide into quadrilaterals around a center vertex, simplexes subdivide into corner simplexes and a central rectified simplex (a tetrahedron becomes 4 tetrahedra and an octahedron), boxes subdivide into 2^N sub-boxes, orthoplexes subdivide into corner orthoplexes and simplex cones (an octahedron becomes 6 octahedra and 8 tetrahedra), and any other cell is subdivided by connecting its centroid to every piece of its subdivided boundary. Elements below the selected ones are always fully subdivided too. Unselected elements above or beside them are conformed by referencing the pieces of their subdivided members, which keeps the mesh crack-free, even under deformation, because the pieces are shared rather than duplicated. Boundary normals, boundary cell vertex normals, and cell texture maps are carried over and interpolated, boundary cells keep their normals and matching orientations, sub-elements of seam elements stay seams, and subdividing volumetric cells creates interior boundary cells that are excluded from rendering. [b]Note:[/b] For the best results, subdivide all desired elements in a single call. A conformed cell is no longer shaped like a simplex, box, or orthoplex, so subdividing it in a later call falls back to the centroid-based subdivision.
